hubs.title: Cryptid costume guides: Bigfoot, Mothman, alien and Yeti
hubs.desc: Costume guides for Bigfoot, Mothman, grey aliens and the Yeti: what witnesses actually described, what to buy and how to build each one yourself.
hubs.lede: Most cryptid costumes are a gorilla suit with a new label. These guides start from what witnesses actually described, then cover what to buy and how to build it yourself.
p: You won't find Wendigo or Skinwalker costume guides here, and that's on purpose. Both belong to living Indigenous traditions, so we don't sell around them. You can read about them, respectfully, on the [Wendigo](/creatures/wendigo/) and [Skinwalker](/creatures/skinwalker/) pages.
Want one we haven't written yet? [Tell us](/contact/) and I'll add it to the list.

articles.title: Bigfoot costume guide: full suits, kids' sizes and a DIY build
articles.blurb: Full fur suits, kids' sizes, inflatables and a build-it-yourself version that gets the head and arms right.
articles.desc: How to pick a Bigfoot or Sasquatch costume that looks like what witnesses actually describe: adult suits, kids' sizes, inflatables and a DIY build from faux fur.
articles.lede: A Bigfoot costume is basically a fur suit and a mask, and most of them get the same couple of things wrong. Here's what to buy, what I'd skip and how to build one yourself for less.

blocks.h: What makes a costume look like Bigfoot
p: Most people buy a gorilla suit and call it a day (and to be fair, from across a parking lot nobody's checking). But if you want it to look like the thing people actually report, the witnesses are pretty consistent about it. They describe something 7 to 9 feet tall with a cone-shaped head, no real neck, long arms and dark brown, black or reddish hair. You can read the full description on our [Bigfoot page](/creatures/bigfoot/).

A gorilla suit has a round head, a bare rubber chest and short arms, which is why it looks like a gorilla. So the parts worth your money are the head shape, the shoulders and the arms. Get those right and a cheap suit looks good. Get them wrong and it doesn't matter what you paid.

blocks.why: These open an Amazon search, so you see what's actually in stock today and not something I picked six months ago.
items: Adult Bigfoot suit
adult bigfoot sasquatch costume full suit
A one-piece fur suit with a separate mask. Check the height range before you order, because a suit that's too short shows your wrists and ankles.
Kids' Bigfoot costume
kids bigfoot sasquatch costume
Usually a hooded fur jumpsuit with an open face, which a kid will keep on a lot longer than a rubber mask.
Inflatable Bigfoot costume
inflatable bigfoot costume adult
A little fan keeps it puffed up, so you get the height and the bulk for free. It's funny, not scary, and that's fine.
Bigfoot mask
bigfoot sasquatch mask
If you're building your own suit, buy the face and make everything else.
Bigfoot feet
bigfoot feet shoe covers costume
It's right there in the name. The feet are the part people look at.
Furry gloves or hands
gorilla hands gloves costume brown
Bare human hands sticking out of a fur sleeve wreck the whole thing in photos.

blocks.h: How to build a Bigfoot costume
p: You can build a better-looking Bigfoot than most store suits with faux fur, some foam and a free weekend. The trick is to build the shape first and worry about the fur second.
items: Start with loose brown or black clothes you don't mind gluing things to. A hooded sweatshirt and sweatpants work.
Pad the shoulders and upper back with foam (or a folded towel pinned inside the hoodie). This hides your neck, and it's the biggest single change you can make.
Build the cone on a ball cap with foam, then pull the hood over it so the head runs straight into the shoulders.
Glue or stitch long-pile faux fur on in overlapping rows from the ankles up, the way shingles go on a roof, so the hair hangs down and covers the seams.
Lengthen the arms. Foam hands on short handles that you hold from inside the sleeves add 15 cm (6 inches) or so, and that's enough to change how you look when you walk.
Make the feet from old slippers with a foam sole glued on. The prints people report run 14 to 18 inches, so go big.

blocks.h: What you need for the DIY build
items: Long-pile faux fur
long pile faux fur fabric brown by the yard
The longer the pile, the better it hides seams. Two to three yards covers most adults.
Upholstery foam sheet
upholstery foam sheet 1 inch
For the shoulders, the cone head and the feet.
Fabric glue or hot glue sticks
fabric glue faux fur
Faster than sewing, and nobody is going to check your stitching.
Brown face paint
brown black face paint kit
If you skip the mask, paint what's left showing so it's dark around the eyes.

p: Fur suits are hot. Really hot. Plan on water breaks and a way to get the head off fast, and if you're walking in a parade in July the inflatable starts to look like the smart choice.

The other one is serious. Please don't wear a Bigfoot suit beside a road, on a trail or in the bush as a prank. In August 2012 a man in Montana put on a camouflage ghillie suit and stood on Highway 93 near Kalispell trying to start a Bigfoot sighting, and he was hit by two cars and killed. His friends told the Highway Patrol that was the whole plan. Hunters are the other reason, for what I hope are obvious reasons. Wear it to the party, the parade or the [festival](/bigfoot-festivals/).

items: What's the difference between a Bigfoot costume and a gorilla costume?

The head, the chest and the arms. Gorilla suits have a round head, a bare chest plate and short arms. Witnesses describe Bigfoot with a pointed head that sits right on the shoulders, hair all over and arms that hang lower than a person's.
What colour should a Bigfoot costume be?
Dark brown is the safe pick. Black and reddish-brown both show up in reports too. White or grey reads as a Yeti, and we have a [Yeti costume guide](/costumes/yeti/) for that.
How do I look taller in a Bigfoot costume?
Go for bulk before height. Padded shoulders and a cone head add about 15 cm and make you look huge. Stilts add more, but you can't see your feet in a fur suit and I wouldn't try it on stairs.
Can I wear a Bigfoot costume to a Bigfoot festival?
Yes, and you won't be the only one. Lots of festivals run a costume contest or a calling contest, so check the event page on our [Bigfoot festivals list](/bigfoot-festivals/) before you go.

articles.title: Mothman costume guide: wings, red eyes and a DIY build
articles.blurb: The red eyes are the whole costume. What to buy, how to build the wings and how to make the eyes glow in photos.
articles.desc: How to put together a Mothman costume: what the 1966 witnesses described, wings and red eyes you can buy, and a simple DIY build with reflectors that glow in photos.
articles.lede: Mothman is one of the easiest cryptids to dress up as, because the whole thing comes down to wings and a pair of red eyes. Here's how to get both right.

p: There are two Mothmen, basically. The first is the one the witnesses reported around Point Pleasant, West Virginia in 1966 and 1967, which was a tall grey figure with wings and big red eyes that glowed in car headlights. Several of them said they couldn't make out a real head at all, just the eyes sitting up near the shoulders. The full story is on our [Mothman page](/creatures/mothman/).

The second is the statue. Bob Roach's stainless steel [Mothman statue](/places/mothman-statue/) in Point Pleasant has a bug face, big muscles and butterfly-style wings, and that's the look most store costumes copy. Pick whichever one you like (the statue version is the one people recognize at a party, to be honest). Either way you need dark wings and red eyes, and everything else is optional.

blocks.h: How to build a Mothman costume
p: This is a one-evening build if you already own dark clothes.
items: Wear dark grey or black from head to toe. A hoodie is perfect because the hood hides the shape of your head.
Make the wings from black or grey fabric cut in a half circle. Stitch or pin the straight edge along the back of each sleeve and down your sides, so the wings open when you lift your arms.

For the eyes, stick two round red bike reflectors on the front of the hood, just above your own eyes. Witnesses said the eyes glowed in headlights, and reflectors do exactly that in a camera flash (which is the photo everybody wants anyway).
If you want them lit all the time, use two battery puck lights with red film taped over them.
Add the fur collar or a ring of fake feathers around the shoulders to blur your neck.
Skip the mask if you can. A dark hood with glowing eyes and no face is closer to the reports and it's a lot easier to breathe in.

blocks.h: Before you walk out the door
p: You're dressed in black from head to toe, at night, probably near a road. Put reflective tape on the back of the wings or carry a light. And LED goggles cut your vision a lot more than you'd think, so try the stairs at home before you try them at somebody's party.

If you want an excuse to wear it more than once, the [Mothman Festival](/places/mothman-festival/) takes over downtown Point Pleasant every September and half the crowd is in costume. Our [Point Pleasant trip guide](/places/point-pleasant-mothman-guide/) covers the statue, the museum and the TNT area.

items: What colour is Mothman?
The 1966 witnesses mostly said grey or brownish grey. Black costumes are more common because black wings are easier to buy, and nobody at the party is going to argue.
Does Mothman have a face?
In the reports, not really. People described two big red eyes set high up, close to the shoulders, and no clear head. The insect face comes from the statue and from later artwork.
How big should the wings be?
Witnesses guessed a wingspan of 10 feet or more. You won't get through a door like that, so aim for wings that reach your fingertips with your arms out.
How do I make Mothman eyes glow?
Red bike reflectors for photos, red LED glasses or puck lights for all night. Reflectors are cheaper and they don't need batteries.

articles.title: Alien costume guide: grey aliens, kids, inflatables and DIY
articles.blurb: Grey alien masks and bodysuits, the inflatable abduction suit, kids' sizes and a face-paint version that takes 20 minutes.
articles.desc: How to pick or build an alien costume: the classic grey alien look from real encounter reports, masks and bodysuits, the inflatable abduction costume, kids' sizes and a quick DIY version.
articles.lede: Green skin and antennae are Hollywood. The alien people actually report is small, grey and has huge black eyes, and it happens to be an easy costume to pull off.
see: Grey aliens: where the look came from

p: In close encounter reports the beings are almost always grey. People describe a short, thin body with no hair, an oversized head, a tiny nose and mouth and big black almond-shaped eyes. That look goes back to Betty and Barney Hill's account from New Hampshire in 1961, and you can read how it spread on our [grey aliens page](/creatures/grey-aliens/).

The "little green men" line is older and mostly a newspaper joke. It got attached to the [Kelly-Hopkinsville case](/encounters/kelly-hopkinsville-1955/) in Kentucky in 1955, even though the family said the things they saw were silvery. So go grey if you want it to look like a real report and green if you want it to look like a cartoon. Both are fine (the kids usually vote green).

p: You don't need a mask for this one. Face paint and a swim cap get you most of the way.
items: Put on a grey or silver swim cap (or a bald cap) to hide your hair and make your head look smooth.
Paint your face, neck and ears grey. Go a shade darker under the cheekbones and down the sides of the nose so your face looks narrower.
For the eyes, paint big black almond shapes around your own eyes, tilted up at the outside corners. Oversized black sunglasses with the arms removed work too, held on with a strip of elastic.
Cover your lips with the same grey so the mouth nearly disappears.
Wear a plain grey or black long-sleeve top and leggings. Grey kitchen gloves finish it off if you didn't buy the long fingers.

p: If you ever wanted to see a few thousand aliens walking down a main street, the [Roswell UFO Festival](/places/roswell-ufo-festival/) runs around the Fourth of July and has a costume parade. Our [Roswell trip guide](/places/roswell-ufo-guide/) has the museum hours and what else is in town. There are smaller UFO Days in the US and Canada too, and they're all on the [UFO festivals list](/ufo-festivals/).

items: What colour should an alien costume be?
Grey if you're going by encounter reports, green if you're going by cartoons. Silver works for a 1950s B-movie look.
How do I do alien eyes without a mask?
Black face paint in a big almond shape around each eye, tilted up at the outer corner. It photographs better than you'd expect.
Is the inflatable alien costume hard to wear?
It runs on a small battery fan, so pack spare batteries. You can't sit down in it very well, and you'll want somebody to help you through doors.
What's a good alien costume for a group?
One abductee in pyjamas and the rest as greys. Or go as the Men in Black, who show up in UFO stories as often as the aliens do.

articles.title: Yeti costume guide: abominable snowman suits and a DIY build
articles.blurb: White fur suits, kids' sizes and inflatables, plus the one detail the reports from the Himalaya get different.
articles.desc: How to pick a Yeti or abominable snowman costume: adult suits, kids' sizes, inflatables and a DIY build, plus what colour the Yeti is in real reports.
articles.lede: A Yeti costume is a Bigfoot costume in white, more or less. It's also about the only costume that works with a winter coat under it.
see: Yeti: tracks, expeditions and DNA tests

blocks.h: The white Yeti is a movie thing
p: Funny enough, the snow-white Yeti mostly comes from cartoons and Christmas specials. The people who've reported one in the Himalaya describe a reddish or grey upright figure, and the famous evidence is all footprints in snow, not sightings of white fur. Our [Yeti page](/creatures/yeti/) has the 1951 Shipton footprint photo story and the DNA tests that pointed at bears.
That said, if you show up in reddish-brown fur everybody will call you Bigfoot all night. So white it is, unless you enjoy explaining things (I do, but I wouldn't recommend it at a party).

p: The build is the same as the one in our [Bigfoot costume guide](/costumes/bigfoot/). Pad the shoulders, build up the head and add fur in rows from the ankles up. Just swap the brown fur for white and start from white or light grey clothes so nothing dark shows through.

If you trick-or-treat anywhere in Canada you already know the costume has to fit over a snowsuit. A Yeti is one of the few where that actually helps, because the extra bulk is the whole point. Size up and nobody will ever know there's a parka in there.

items: Is a Yeti the same as the abominable snowman?
Yes. "Abominable Snowman" came from a 1921 newspaper mistranslation of a Himalayan name, and it stuck.
What colour is a Yeti?
White in the movies. Reddish-brown or grey in most of the reports from Nepal and Tibet.
What's the difference between a Yeti costume and a Bigfoot costume?
Colour, mostly. Yeti suits are white with a pale blue or grey face and Bigfoot suits are brown or black. The shape is the same.
How do I keep a white fur costume clean?
You don't, really. Spot clean it with a damp cloth, brush the fur out when it's dry and store it in a bag.

articles.title: Bigfoot gifts: shirts, statues, stickers and ideas that get used
articles.blurb: Shirts, garden statues, stickers, toys and a few gifts that are better than more stuff.
articles.desc: Bigfoot gift ideas that actually get used: shirts, garden statues, stickers, plush toys and socks, plus books, festival trips and a track casting kit for the serious ones.
articles.lede: Buying for somebody who loves Bigfoot is easy because there's a Sasquatch version of nearly everything. Here's the stuff that gets used, and a few ideas that aren't stuff at all.

p: There are two kinds of Bigfoot people. The first kind thinks Sasquatch is funny and wants him on a mug. The second kind has a trail camera strapped to a tree right now and will tell you about it. Figure out which one you've got before you spend anything, because the mug person doesn't want plaster and the trail camera person already owns six shirts.
For the first kind, scroll down a bit. For the second kind, skip to the last section.

p: Nearly every statue, sticker and shirt uses the same pose, with the figure in mid-stride looking back over its shoulder. That's frame 352 of the film Roger Patterson and Bob Gimlin shot at Bluff Creek, California in 1967. So if your Bigfoot person asks whether you know where the pose comes from, now you do (and they will ask).

blocks.h: Gifts for somebody who actually goes looking
blocks.why: This is the person with the trail camera. Buy them something they'll take into the woods. Our [casting guide](/guides/casting-tracks/) shows how to cast a print, and there's more on the [field gear page](/gear/).
items: Track casting kit supplies
dental stone casting
Dental stone is what trackers use to cast prints, and it holds more detail than plaster of Paris.
Red-light headlamp
red light headlamp
Keeps their night vision and doesn't light up the whole hillside.
Photo scale ruler
forensic photo scale ruler
A track photo without a scale in it is just a photo of a hole.
Handheld audio recorder
handheld digital audio recorder
Howls and wood knocks are the most common evidence, and a phone mic misses most of it.

p: If they've already got the shirt and the statue, buy the trip. A weekend at a [Bigfoot festival](/bigfoot-festivals/) costs less than you'd think and most of them are free to walk around. There are [Bigfoot museums](/places/museums/) in more places than you'd guess, and a few outfits run [guided expeditions](/expeditions/) if you want to go all in.
Books are the other easy win. We keep a list of the good ones, skeptical and believing, on the [books page](/books/).

items: What do you get a Bigfoot fan who has everything?
A trip. A festival weekend, a museum visit or a guided night hike beats one more thing for the shelf.
What is a good cheap Bigfoot gift?
Stickers or socks. Both cost a few dollars and both get used.
Are Bigfoot statues weatherproof?
Resin ones usually handle rain but fade in full sun, and metal silhouettes last longest. Read the listing, because it changes from one maker to the next.
What are good Bigfoot gifts for kids?
A plush, a sticker pack, or a plaster casting kit they can use on dog tracks in the backyard.

articles.title: Mothman gifts: plush, statues, shirts and the book to start with
articles.blurb: Plushies, statue replicas, shirts and pins, plus the book and the trip a real Mothman fan wants.
articles.desc: Mothman gift ideas: plush toys, statue replicas, shirts, pins and stickers, plus the book to start with and a trip to Point Pleasant for the fan who has everything.
articles.lede: Mothman merch has gone from one shop in West Virginia to pretty much everywhere. Here's what's worth buying, and where the money does the most good.

blocks.h: Buy from Point Pleasant if you can
p: The [Mothman Museum](/places/mothman-museum/) in Point Pleasant runs its own shop, in person and online, and a purchase there keeps the lights on at the only Mothman museum in the world. I'd look there first for shirts and anything with the statue on it.
For everything else, or if you need it by Friday, Amazon has plenty.

p: Bob Roach built the stainless steel [Mothman statue](/places/mothman-statue/) that has stood in downtown Point Pleasant since 2003. He gave it a very athletic build, the internet noticed the back of it, and there are now pins, stickers and shirts about that view in particular. I'm not going to tell you what to search for. You'll find it.
If you're buying a replica, the real one is about 12 feet tall with the wings spread and red eyes, so that's what a good copy looks like.

John Keel's The Mothman Prophecies (1975) is the book that made Mothman famous, and the 2002 movie is based on it. It's strange and it wanders all over the place, and a real fan will want it anyway. It's on our [books page](/books/) with the others.

The best Mothman gift is a weekend in Point Pleasant. The museum is $4.99 to get in, the statue is free and the [Mothman Festival](/places/mothman-festival/) fills the town every September. Our [Point Pleasant trip guide](/places/point-pleasant-mothman-guide/) has the hours and a plan for the day.

items: Where can I buy official Mothman merchandise?
The Mothman Museum in Point Pleasant, West Virginia has a shop in the building and an online store. Buying there supports the museum.
What is a good Mothman gift for a kid?
A plush. The reports from 1966 are pretty scary and the plush is not.
Is there a Mothman book?
Start with The Mothman Prophecies by John Keel. Jeff Wamsley, who runs the museum, has written books that collect the original witness accounts and newspaper clippings.
What do you get a Mothman fan who has everything?
A trip to Point Pleasant in September for the festival.

articles.title: Things to do in Roswell, NM: UFO museum, alien stops, day plan
articles.h1: Things to do in Roswell, New Mexico
articles.desc: What to do in Roswell, New Mexico: the International UFO Museum (hours and prices), the flying saucer McDonald's, the UFO Festival, Bottomless Lakes and a one-day plan.
articles.lede: Roswell is a small city that went all in on one week in July 1947. You can see the UFO stuff in a day, and there's more to do nearby than most people expect.

p: In the summer of 1947 a rancher named Mac Brazel found a field of strange debris on a ranch northwest of town. On July 8 the Roswell Army Air Field put out a press release saying it had recovered a "flying disc". The next day the Army said it was a weather balloon. The Air Force said in the 1990s that it was a secret balloon project called Mogul, and plenty of people don't buy that either. Our [Roswell 1947 case page](/ufo/cases/roswell-1947/) goes through what's known.

Here's the thing to know before you drive. The debris field isn't in Roswell. It's about 75 miles northwest near Corona, on open range, and there's not much to look at. The town is where the museum, the shops and the alien-eyed streetlights are (yes, the streetlights on Main Street have alien eyes).

blocks.h: UFO things to do in Roswell
p: The [International UFO Museum](/places/international-ufo-museum/) is the main event and it's right downtown at 114 North Main Street. It's open every day from 9 to 5, and admission is $7 for adults and $4 for kids 5 to 15. Give it an hour or two. Most of the alien gift shops are within a couple of blocks, so park once and walk.

Bottomless Lakes State Park is 15 miles southeast of town and it's the best non-alien thing here. It's a chain of eight small lakes that are really sinkholes, from 17 to 90 feet deep, with swimming and paddleboard rentals at Lea Lake in summer. After a morning of alien dioramas it's a nice change.

One heads-up. The Roswell Museum, which holds a rebuilt version of Robert Goddard's rocket workshop (he did his liquid-fuel rocket work near Roswell in the 1930s), was badly damaged in the October 2024 flood. It was still closed the last time we checked, in the fall of 2026, so look it up before you plan around it.

blocks.kick: If you only have a day
items: Morning: the UFO Museum when it opens at 9, before the tour buses.
Late morning: walk Main Street for the gift shops, the murals and the streetlights.
Lunch: the flying saucer McDonald's on North Main if you've got kids with you (it's a McDonald's, but it's shaped like a UFO, so you kind of have to).
Afternoon: Bottomless Lakes for a swim in summer. In winter, take your time in the gift shops instead.
Evening: back downtown after dark, when the neon and the alien streetlights are on.

blocks.h: Festival week or a quiet week?
p: The [Roswell UFO Festival](/places/roswell-ufo-festival/) runs around the Fourth of July with a costume parade, a drone show and speakers at the museum. It's the most fun week to be there and also the hottest and the most crowded, so book a room early. If you'd sooner have the museum to yourself, spring and fall are easier. Thinking of dressing up? We've got an [alien costume guide](/costumes/alien/).

items: How much time do you need in Roswell?
One full day covers the UFO museum, downtown and one extra stop. Add a second day if you want a proper afternoon at Bottomless Lakes.
Can you visit the Roswell crash site?

The debris field is on ranch land near Corona, about 75 miles northwest of Roswell. There's a spot on public land tied to the story, listed as the [UFO skip site](/places/ufo-skip-site/), and it's hike-in only.
What are the UFO museum hours in Roswell?
9 am to 5 pm every day. It's closed on Thanksgiving, Christmas Day and New Year's Day and shuts at 2 pm the day before each.
Is Roswell worth visiting if you are not into UFOs?
For a few hours, sure. Bottomless Lakes is a good stop on its own, and the town is fun to walk around even if you think the whole thing was a balloon.

articles.title: Point Pleasant, WV Mothman trip: statue, museum and TNT area
articles.desc: How to do a Mothman trip to Point Pleasant, West Virginia: the Mothman statue, the Mothman Museum (hours and prices), TNT area tours, the September festival and a half-day plan.
articles.lede: Point Pleasant is a small river town in West Virginia that turned one strange year into a whole identity. You can see all of the Mothman stops in half a day, and they're all within a short walk or drive.

p: On November 15, 1966 two young couples driving past the old explosives plant north of town said a tall grey thing with wings and red eyes chased their car. Dozens of other people reported it over the next year. Then on December 15, 1967 the Silver Bridge over the Ohio River collapsed in rush-hour traffic and 46 people died, and the two stories have been tied together ever since. Our [Mothman page](/creatures/mothman/) has the long version.
The town took a while to lean into it. Now there's a statue, a museum and a festival, and Mothman is on pretty much every shop window on Main Street.

Start downtown. The [Mothman statue](/places/mothman-statue/) is free and it's the photo everybody takes. The [Mothman Museum](/places/mothman-museum/) is a few steps away at 400 Main Street. It's open Monday to Thursday 10 to 5, Friday and Saturday 10 to 6 and Sunday noon to 5, and it costs $4.99 (or $1.99 for kids 10 and under). The museum also sells the guided tours of the TNT area, where the first sighting happened.

Tu-Endie-Wei State Park sits right where the Kanawha River meets the Ohio, a short walk from the statue. It has an 84-foot granite monument to the 1774 Battle of Point Pleasant and it's open all year. It's also the best spot in town to look at the river and see where the Silver Bridge crossed.

The bridge is the part of the story I'd slow down for. The collapse was traced to a crack in a single steel eyebar, about a tenth of an inch deep, and it changed how bridges get inspected across the US. Whatever you think people saw in 1966, 46 people from a small town died that night, and the town remembers them.

blocks.kick: If you only have half a day
items: Park downtown and get your photo with the statue first, before the crowd.
Do the museum next. An hour is plenty for most people, longer if you read every clipping (I would).
Walk to Tu-Endie-Wei and the riverfront. It's about ten minutes on foot.
Drive north to the TNT area for the concrete igloos, or book the guided tour through the museum if you'd like somebody to show you where things happened.
Back downtown for a late lunch and the gift shops.

blocks.h: Festival weekend or a quiet day?
p: The [Mothman Festival](/places/mothman-festival/) happens every September and it's free. It's also packed, and rooms in town book up months ahead. If you want the costumes, the vendors and the hayrides, go then. If you want to read the museum displays in peace, pick any other weekend. Going in costume? Here's our [Mothman costume guide](/costumes/mothman/), and the [gift guide](/gifts/mothman/) covers what to bring home.

items: How long do you need in Point Pleasant?
Half a day covers the statue, the museum and the riverfront. Add a couple of hours for the TNT area.
How much is the Mothman Museum?
$4.99 for ages 11 and up and $1.99 for kids 10 and under. They take Visa, MasterCard and cash.
Is the Mothman statue free to visit?
Yes. It's outdoors in downtown Point Pleasant and you can walk up to it any time.
Can you visit the TNT area on your own?
Yes. It's public land north of town and the old concrete igloos are still there. The guided tours sold through the Mothman Museum are the easier way to find the right spots.
